interest: It documents how the occupation reported narcotics control to international bodies, including seizure details, statistics, Korean regulations and 1945 War Crimes Office efforts to prepare narcotics treaty-violation charges against Japan.
overview: This 202-page file records US handling of narcotics control in occupied Japan and South Korea from 1944 to 1948. It includes SCAP seizure reports, statistical returns to the Permanent Central Opium Board and the UN, and War Crimes Office evidence gathering on Japan's treaty violations. It also holds narcotics regulations and peace-treaty proposals.
